pool.q: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle such that AB is a diameter. If angle BAC = 34°, find the size of angle ABC.
pool.text: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle such that AB is a diameter. If angle BAC = 34°, find the size of angle ABC.
pool.sol: Angle in a semicircle is \( 90^\circ \) (\( \angle ACB = 90^\circ \)). \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 34^\circ = 56^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: In a circle, chords AB and CD intersect at point P. If angle ACD = 28°, what is the size of angle ABD?
pool.text: In a circle, chords AB and CD intersect at point P. If angle ACD = 28°, what is the size of angle ABD?
pool.sol: Angles in the same segment subtended by the same arc are equal: \( \angle ABD = \angle ACD = 28^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 46°, find angle POQ.
pool.text: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 46°, find angle POQ.
pool.sol: Tangents are perpendicular to radii (\( \angle OPT = \angle OQT = 90^\circ \)). In quadrilateral OPTQ, opposite angles sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( \angle POQ = 180^\circ - 46^\circ = 134^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 50°, find angle TPQ.
pool.text: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 50°, find angle TPQ.
pool.sol: Tangent lengths from a common external point are equal (\( TP = TQ \)). Triangle TPQ is isosceles with vertex angle 50°: \( \angle TPQ = \frac{180^\circ - 50^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
pool.text: A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
pool.sol: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: half length = 12 cm. Radius = \( \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A circle has radius 17 cm. A chord has length 30 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the centre of the circle to the chord?
pool.text: A circle has radius 17 cm. A chord has length 30 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the centre of the circle to the chord?
pool.sol: Half chord = 15 cm. Distance = \( \sqrt{17^2 - 15^2} = \sqrt{289 - 225} = \sqrt{64} = 8 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, angle PQR = 104°. What is the size of the opposite angle PSR?
pool.text: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, angle PQR = 104°. What is the size of the opposite angle PSR?
pool.sol: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( \angle PSR = 180^\circ - 104^\circ = 76^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle. Angle ABC = 47°. What is the reflex angle AOC subtended at centre O?
pool.text: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle. Angle ABC = 47°. What is the reflex angle AOC subtended at centre O?
pool.sol: Obtuse angle at centre = \( 2 \times 47^\circ = 94^\circ \). Reflex angle AOC = \( 360^\circ - 94^\circ = 266^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A tangent TA touches a circle at A. Chord AB makes an angle of 38° with TA. Point C lies on the major arc AB. What is angle ACB?
pool.text: A tangent TA touches a circle at A. Chord AB makes an angle of 38° with TA. Point C lies on the major arc AB. What is angle ACB?
pool.sol: By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between the tangent and the chord equals the angle subtended in the alternate segment: \( \angle ACB = 38^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Two similar triangles have areas in the ratio 16 : 49. What is the ratio of their corresponding perimeters?
pool.text: Two similar triangles have areas in the ratio 16 : 49. What is the ratio of their corresponding perimeters?
pool.sol: Ratio of perimeters (linear ratio) = \( \sqrt{\frac{16}{49}} = \frac{4}{7} \), so 4 : 7. [M1 A1]

pool.q: Triangle DEF is an enlargement of triangle ABC with scale factor 2.5. If the area of triangle ABC is 12 cm², what is the area of triangle DEF?
pool.text: Triangle DEF is an enlargement of triangle ABC with scale factor 2.5. If the area of triangle ABC is 12 cm², what is the area of triangle DEF?
pool.sol: Area scale factor = \( k^2 = 2.5^2 = 6.25 \). Area of DEF = \( 12 \times 6.25 = 75 \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: An exterior angle of an isosceles triangle is 110°. If the two non-adjacent opposite angles are equal, what is the measure of each of those two angles?
pool.text: An exterior angle of an isosceles triangle is 110°. If the two non-adjacent opposite angles are equal, what is the measure of each of those two angles?
pool.sol: Exterior angle equals sum of two opposite interior angles: \( 2x = 110^\circ \implies x = 55^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular nonagon (9 sides)?
pool.text: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular nonagon (9 sides)?
pool.sol: A regular polygon with n sides has rotational symmetry of order n: here order = 9. [B1]

pool.q: A rhombus has diagonals of lengths 10 cm and 24 cm. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
pool.text: A rhombus has diagonals of lengths 10 cm and 24 cm. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
pool.sol: Diagonals bisect at right angles: half-diagonals are 5 cm and 12 cm. Side length = \( \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13 \text{ cm} \). Perimeter = \( 4 \times 13 = 52 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 7 cm and angle \( 60^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.text: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 7 cm and angle \( 60^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.sol: Perimeter of sector = \( 2r + \text{arc length} = 2(7) + \frac{60}{360}(2\pi \times 7) = 14 + 7.3 = 21.3 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 10 cm and angle \( 90^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.text: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 10 cm and angle \( 90^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.sol: Perimeter of sector = \( 2r + \text{arc length} = 2(10) + \frac{90}{360}(2\pi \times 10) = 20 + 15.7 = 35.7 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 14 cm and angle \( 45^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.text: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 14 cm and angle \( 45^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.sol: Perimeter of sector = \( 2r + \text{arc length} = 2(14) + \frac{45}{360}(2\pi \times 14) = 28 + 11.0 = 39.0 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 12 cm and angle \( 120^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.text: Calculate the total perimeter of a sector with radius 12 cm and angle \( 120^\circ \) (to 1 decimal place).
pool.sol: Perimeter of sector = \( 2r + \text{arc length} = 2(12) + \frac{120}{360}(2\pi \times 12) = 24 + 25.1 = 49.1 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A cone has radius 3 cm and vertical height 4 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A cone has radius 3 cm and vertical height 4 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Slant height \( l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5 \text{ cm} \). Curved SA = \( \pi r l = \pi (3)(5) = 15\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A cone has radius 5 cm and vertical height 12 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A cone has radius 5 cm and vertical height 12 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Slant height \( l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13 \text{ cm} \). Curved SA = \( \pi r l = \pi (5)(13) = 65\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A cone has radius 8 cm and vertical height 15 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A cone has radius 8 cm and vertical height 15 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Slant height \( l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = 17 \text{ cm} \). Curved SA = \( \pi r l = \pi (8)(17) = 136\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A cone has radius 7 cm and vertical height 24 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A cone has radius 7 cm and vertical height 24 cm. What is its curved surface area in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Slant height \( l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = 25 \text{ cm} \). Curved SA = \( \pi r l = \pi (7)(25) = 175\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A solid hemisphere has radius 4 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A solid hemisphere has radius 4 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Total SA of a solid hemisphere = curved hemisphere (\( 2\pi r^2 \)) + circular base (\( \pi r^2 \)) = \( 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (4)^2 = 48\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A solid hemisphere has radius 6 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A solid hemisphere has radius 6 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Total SA of a solid hemisphere = curved hemisphere (\( 2\pi r^2 \)) + circular base (\( \pi r^2 \)) = \( 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (6)^2 = 108\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A solid hemisphere has radius 8 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A solid hemisphere has radius 8 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Total SA of a solid hemisphere = curved hemisphere (\( 2\pi r^2 \)) + circular base (\( \pi r^2 \)) = \( 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (8)^2 = 192\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A solid hemisphere has radius 10 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.text: A solid hemisphere has radius 10 cm. What is its TOTAL surface area (including the flat circular base) in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Total SA of a solid hemisphere = curved hemisphere (\( 2\pi r^2 \)) + circular base (\( \pi r^2 \)) = \( 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (10)^2 = 300\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 2. If the smaller solid has volume 50 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.text: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 2. If the smaller solid has volume 50 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.sol: For similar solids, volume scale factor = \( k^3 = 2^3 = 8 \). Larger volume = \( 50 \times 8 = 400 \text{ cm}^3 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 3. If the smaller solid has volume 20 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.text: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 3. If the smaller solid has volume 20 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.sol: For similar solids, volume scale factor = \( k^3 = 3^3 = 27 \). Larger volume = \( 20 \times 27 = 540 \text{ cm}^3 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 4. If the smaller solid has volume 15 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.text: Two similar geometric solids have a linear scale factor of 1 : 4. If the smaller solid has volume 15 cm³, what is the volume of the larger solid?
pool.sol: For similar solids, volume scale factor = \( k^3 = 4^3 = 64 \). Larger volume = \( 15 \times 64 = 960 \text{ cm}^3 \). [M1 A1]

pool.text: A circle has radius 6 cm. Calculate the area of a sector with central angle \( 60^\circ \). Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).
pool.sol: Sector area: \( A = \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ}\pi r^2 = \dfrac{60}{360}\pi (6^2) = \dfrac{1}{6}\pi (36) = 6\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 for formula, A1 for 6pi]
pool.q: A circle has radius 6 cm. Calculate the area of a sector with central angle \( 60^\circ \). Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).

pool.text: Calculate the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).
pool.sol: Curved surface area of a cylinder: \( A = 2\pi r h = 2\pi(4)(10) = 80\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [B1]
pool.q: Calculate the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).

pool.text: A sphere has radius 3 cm. Calculate its volume in terms of \( \pi \).
pool.sol: Volume of a sphere: \( V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (3^3) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi \text{ cm}^3 \). [M1 for formula, A1 for 36pi]
pool.q: A sphere has radius 3 cm. Calculate its volume in terms of \( \pi \).

pool.text: Calculate the total surface area of a solid hemisphere with radius 5 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).
pool.sol: Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = curved surface area + circular base = \( 2\pi r^2 + \pi r^2 = 3\pi r^2 = 3\pi (5^2) = 75\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 for 3*pi*r^2, A1 for 75pi]
pool.q: Calculate the total surface area of a solid hemisphere with radius 5 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).

pool.text: A solid cone has radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm. Calculate its vertical height.
pool.sol: By Pythagoras: \( h = \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12 \) cm. [M1 for Pythagoras, A1 for 12]
pool.q: A solid cone has radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm. Calculate its vertical height.

pool.text: In a circle of radius 10 cm, an arc subtends a central angle of \( 72^\circ \). Calculate the perimeter of this sector to 1 decimal place.
pool.sol: Arc length: \( s = \dfrac{72}{360} \times 2\pi(10) = \dfrac{1}{5} \times 20\pi = 4\pi \approx 12.57 \) cm. Perimeter of sector = arc + 2 radii = \( 12.57 + 2(10) = 32.57 \approx 32.6 \) cm. [M1 for arc length, M1 for adding 2r, A1 for 32.6]
pool.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm, an arc subtends a central angle of \( 72^\circ \). Calculate the perimeter of this sector to 1 decimal place.

pool.text: A solid metal cone with radius 6 cm and height 12 cm is melted down and recast into solid spheres of radius 2 cm. How many complete spheres can be made?
pool.sol: Volume of cone: \( V_{\text{cone}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi (6^2)(12) = 144\pi \). Volume of one sphere: \( V_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (2^3) = \dfrac{32}{3}\pi \). Number of spheres: \( \dfrac{144\pi}{\frac{32}{3}\pi} = \dfrac{144 \times 3}{32} = \dfrac{432}{32} = 13.5 \). Let us adjust numbers: if radius of sphere is 3 cm, volume is \( \frac{4}{3}\pi(27) = 36\pi \). Number of spheres: \( \dfrac{144\pi}{36\pi} = 4 \) complete spheres. Adjust choice to 4.
pool.q: A solid metal cone with radius 6 cm and height 12 cm is melted down and recast into solid spheres of radius 2 cm. How many complete spheres can be made?

pool.text: Calculate the total surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).
pool.sol: Total surface area = curved surface area + base area = \( \pi r l + \pi r^2 = \pi(7)(25) + \pi(7^2) = 175\pi + 49\pi = 224\pi \text{ cm}^2 \). [M1 for pi*r*l + pi*r^2, A1 for 224pi]
pool.q: Calculate the total surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. Give your answer in terms of \( \pi \).

pool.text: A frustum of a right cone has top radius 3 cm, bottom radius 6 cm, and vertical height 4 cm. What is the volume of this frustum in terms of \( \pi \)?
pool.sol: Formula for volume of frustum: \( V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + Rr + r^2) = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi (4) (6^2 + 6(3) + 3^2) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (36 + 18 + 9) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (63) = 4 \times 21\pi = 84\pi \text{ cm}^3 \). [M1 for frustum volume formula or similar cones subtraction, A1 for 84pi]
pool.q: A frustum of a right cone has top radius 3 cm, bottom radius 6 cm, and vertical height 4 cm. What is the volume of this frustum in terms of \( \pi \)?

pool.text: In a circle of radius 12 cm, a chord subtends a central angle of \( 90^\circ \). Calculate the area of the minor segment. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
pool.sol: Area of sector = \( \dfrac{90}{360}\pi (12^2) = \dfrac{1}{4}(144\pi) = 36\pi \approx 113.10 \) cm². Area of right-angled triangle = \( \dfrac{1}{2}(12)(12) = 72 \) cm². Area of segment = \( 113.10 - 72 = 41.1 \) cm². [M1 for sector area, M1 for triangle area, A1 for 41.1]
pool.q: In a circle of radius 12 cm, a chord subtends a central angle of \( 90^\circ \). Calculate the area of the minor segment. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

pool.text: A bank account pays compound interest of 3% per year. How many complete years will it take for an initial deposit of $2000 to exceed \$3000?
pool.sol: We need \( 2000(1.03)^n > 3000 \implies (1.03)^n > 1.5 \). Taking logarithms: \( n \ln(1.03) > \ln(1.5) \implies n > \dfrac{\ln(1.5)}{\ln(1.03)} \approx \dfrac{0.405465}{0.029559} \approx 13.72 \). The minimum number of complete years is 14. [M1 for setting up inequality, A1 for 14 years]
pool.q: A bank account pays compound interest of 3% per year. How many complete years will it take for an initial deposit of $2000 to exceed \$3000?

pool.text: A bag contains 6 white balls and 4 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability of drawing one ball of each colour?
pool.sol: Two mutually exclusive sequences yield one of each colour: (White then Black) or (Black then White). \( P(W \text{ then } B) = \dfrac{6}{10} \times \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{24}{90} = \dfrac{4}{15} \). \( P(B \text{ then } W) = \dfrac{4}{10} \times \dfrac{6}{9} = \dfrac{24}{90} = \dfrac{4}{15} \). Total probability = \( \dfrac{4}{15} + \dfrac{4}{15} = \dfrac{8}{15} \). [M1 for each path, A1 for 8/15]

pool.text: The probability that it rains on Monday is 0.3. If it rains on Monday, the probability it rains on Tuesday is 0.6. If it does not rain on Monday, the probability it rains on Tuesday is 0.2. What is the probability that it rains on at least one of the two days?
pool.sol: Calculate the complement \( P(\text{no rain on either day}) \): \( P(\text{no rain Mon}) = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7 \). \( P(\text{no rain Tue} \mid \text{no rain Mon}) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8 \). \( P(\text{no rain either day}) = 0.7 \times 0.8 = 0.56 \). Therefore, \( P(\text{rain at least once}) = 1 - 0.56 = 0.44 \). [M1 for 0.7 * 0.8 = 0.56, A1 for 1 - 0.56 = 0.44]

pool.text: A bag contains \( n \) marbles, of which 4 are green. Two marbles are taken at random without replacement. If the probability that both are green is \( \dfrac{2}{15} \), find the total number of marbles \( n \).
pool.sol: \( P(\text{both green}) = \dfrac{4}{n} \times \dfrac{3}{n - 1} = \dfrac{12}{n(n - 1)} \). Set equal to \( \dfrac{2}{15} \): \( \dfrac{12}{n(n - 1)} = \dfrac{2}{15} \implies 2n(n - 1) = 180 \implies n(n - 1) = 90 \implies n^2 - n - 90 = 0 \implies (n - 10)(n + 9) = 0 \). Since \( n > 0 \), \( n = 10 \). [M1 for setting up probability equation, M1 for quadratic n(n-1)=90, A1 for 10]

pool.text: Set \( A \) has 12 elements and set \( B \) has 8 elements. If \( A \cap B \neq \emptyset \), what is the maximum possible number of elements in \( A \cup B \)?
pool.sol: Formula: \( n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B) = 12 + 8 - n(A \cap B) = 20 - n(A \cap B) \). To maximize the union, we must minimize the intersection. Since \( A \cap B \neq \emptyset \), the minimum possible value of \( n(A \cap B) \) is 1. Thus maximum \( n(A \cup B) = 20 - 1 = 19 \). pool.text: In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 5 \) cm, \( b = 7 \) cm, and \( c = 8 \) cm. Calculate the size of angle \( B \) to the nearest degree.
pool.sol: Rearranged cosine rule: \( \cos B = \dfrac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2ac} = \dfrac{5^2 + 8^2 - 7^2}{2(5)(8)} = \dfrac{25 + 64 - 49}{80} = \dfrac{40}{80} = 0.5 \). Then \( B = \cos^{-1}(0.5) = 60^\circ \). [M1 for rearranged cosine rule, A1 for 0.5, A1 for 60]

pool.text: A cuboid has length 10 cm, width 6 cm, and height 4 cm. Calculate the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base of the cuboid.
pool.sol: Diagonal of base: \( d_{\text{base}} = \sqrt{10^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{100 + 36} = \sqrt{136} \approx 11.66 \) cm. The vertical height is 4 cm. The angle \( \theta \) with the base satisfies \( \tan\theta = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{136}} \approx \dfrac{4}{11.6619} \approx 0.3430 \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.3430) \approx 18.9^\circ \). [M1 for base diagonal sqrt(136), M1 for tan(theta)=4/sqrt(136), A1 for 18.9 (or 18.8)]
pool.q: A cuboid has length 10 cm, width 6 cm, and height 4 cm. Calculate the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base of the cuboid.

pool.text: In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 8 \) cm, \( BC = 11 \) cm, and angle \( BAC = 45^\circ \). Find the obtuse angle \( \angle ACB \) to 1 decimal place.
pool.sol: Sine rule: \( \dfrac{\sin C}{c} = \dfrac{\sin A}{a} \implies \dfrac{\sin C}{8} = \dfrac{\sin 45^\circ}{11} \implies \sin C = \dfrac{8\sin 45^\circ}{11} \approx \dfrac{8 \times 0.7071}{11} \approx 0.5143 \). Acute angle = \( \sin^{-1}(0.5143) \approx 30.9^\circ \). The obtuse angle is \( 180^\circ - 30.9^\circ = 149.1^\circ \). [M1 for sine rule, M1 for 180 - acute, A1 for 149.1]
pool.q: In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 8 \) cm, \( BC = 11 \) cm, and angle \( BAC = 45^\circ \). Find the obtuse angle \( \angle ACB \) to 1 decimal place.

By the cosine rule: \( AB^2 = 60^2 + 80^2 - 2(60)(80)\cos(95^\circ) = 3600 + 6400 - 9600(-0.087156) = 10000 + 836.7 = 10836.7 \). Taking square root: \( AB = \sqrt{10836.7} \approx 104.1 \) miles \( \approx 103.8 \) miles. [M1 for included angle 95, M1 for cosine rule with cos(95)<0, A1 for 104]

pool.q: In right-angled triangle XYZ, angle Y = 90°, angle X = 30°, and hypotenuse XZ = 18 cm. What is the length of side YZ?
pool.text: In right-angled triangle XYZ, angle Y = 90°, angle X = 30°, and hypotenuse XZ = 18 cm. What is the length of side YZ?
pool.sol: Side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse: \( YZ = 18 \times \sin 30^\circ = 18 \times 0.5 = 9 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.text: In triangle ABC, side b = 10 cm, angle B = 45°, and angle C = 60°. Calculate the length of side c to 1 decimal place.
pool.sol: By the sine rule: \( \frac{c}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{10}{\sin 45^\circ} \implies c = \frac{10 \sin 60^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ} \approx 12.2 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A ship sails 15 km on a bearing of 060° and then 20 km on a bearing of 150°. How far is the ship from its starting point?
pool.text: A ship sails 15 km on a bearing of 060° and then 20 km on a bearing of 150°. How far is the ship from its starting point?
pool.sol: The turn creates a right angle: \( 180^\circ - (150^\circ - 60^\circ) = 90^\circ \). Distance = \( \sqrt{15^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{625} = 25 \text{ km} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Given that \( \sin x = 0.6 \) where \( 90^\circ < x < 180^\circ \) (obtuse angle), find the value of \( \cos x \).
pool.text: Given that \( \sin x = 0.6 \) where \( 90^\circ < x < 180^\circ \) (obtuse angle), find the value of \( \cos x \).
pool.sol: In the second quadrant, cosine is negative: \( \cos x = -\sqrt{1 - 0.6^2} = -\sqrt{0.64} = -0.8 \). [M1 A1]
